_comment: EACH STDIO SERVER RUNS DIRECTLY WHERE ITS BINARY EXISTS. A workstation that
has the binary execs it at once and is unchanged; where it is absent, what
happens next depends on whether anything is going to install it.
`serena` WAITS REMOTELY, `docker` DOES NOT. .github/scripts/cloud-bootstrap.sh
installs serena and a remote session can start before it has finished, so
that wrapper waits for the binary to appear. Nothing installs `uvx`, and
there is no dockerd socket to reach in the sandbox either, so a wait there
would stall three minutes and fail with exactly the error it started from.
NEVER `exit 0` ON A WORKSTATION. The obvious wrapper — exit 0 unless the
remote marker is set — makes every stdio server remote-only, which would
silently disable the two that work here today. A workstation missing the
binary exits NON-ZERO and fails to connect, exactly as it does without any
wrapper: a server that is meant to be there and is not must say so.
`sonarqube` is http rather than stdio, so nothing is installed for it and no
wrapper applies. Its headers are the WORKSTATION's and are deliberately
unconditional: remotely the credential proxy attaches the token for that
host, and whether it OVERRIDES a header the client sends or requires it
absent is not yet measured — design D6 records that as the question the
first remote session settles. Guessing a `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE` conditional
here would encode an answer nobody has; if the proxy needs the header
absent, the fix is one line and it lands with the measurement.

args: command -v uvx >/dev/null 2>&1 && exec uvx mcp-server-docker; exit 1

command -v serena >/dev/null 2>&1 && exec serena start-mcp-server --context claude-code --project-from-cwd; [ "$CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE" = "1" ] || [ "$CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE" = "true" ] || exit 1; for _ in $(seq 180); do command -v serena >/dev/null 2>&1 && exec serena start-mcp-server --context claude-code --project-from-cwd; sleep 1; done; exit 1
